paragraphs: Including the cabin and working doors changes what an airliner asset can do. Boarding shots, cabin interiors, safety material and turnaround sequences all become possible from one file rather than needing a separate interior build, and the doors mean the aircraft can be shown open on stand.

It is a large asset at 2,405,109 polygons and 2,473,953 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and that weight is where the interior lives: seats, bins, sidewalls and galley all modelled rather than implied behind tinted windows.

Three rigged builds share this page at $449, including versions prepared for Cinema 4D and for Maya. The static model at $349 covers airline marketing, airport visualisation, safety and training material, film and television, and news graphics.

A service robot is only convincing in motion. Standing still it is an appliance; walking, turning its head or handing something over it becomes an assistant, and that difference is entirely animation. This set arrives rigged and animated, prepared for Maya, with the deformation already solved.
Supplying several robots as a set also lets a scene show a fleet rather than one unit, which is how the technology is actually deployed in warehouses, hotels and hospitals.

At $349 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits robotics and automation marketing, future of work and service industry presentation, technology journalism, previsualisation and games. On sale since 2026.

The shortest variant of this family in a low cost livery is an unusual and useful combination, and this build includes the cabin. The short fuselage changes the proportions noticeably: fewer window rows and a wing that looks large relative to the body compared with the stretched versions.

It is one of the heaviest aircraft assets in the catalogue at 4,409,964 polygons and 4,567,247 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. That density is the interior, built to the same standard as the exterior.

This page carries a second static build at $349 and rigged versions at $449. Aimed at airline marketing, airport visualisation, safety and training material, film and television, and news graphics. On sale since 2025.

A corrections transport is a bus rebuilt for security: barred or meshed windows, a cage partition behind the driver, a secure rear door and seating without amenities. Including an officer and a person being transported turns the vehicle into a scene that explains a process rather than showing hardware.
The mesh runs 442,621 polygons and 482,062 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, covering the vehicle, the interior and both figures.

At $339 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits criminal justice and corrections visualisation, documentary and news graphics, film and television, policy and training material, and games. On sale since 2025.

Three engines on a business jet is now unusual, and this aircraft is the reason the layout survived: the centre engine gives transoceanic reliability that twins took decades to match. That trijet tail is the identification, and it makes the rear of the aircraft unlike anything else on a modern ramp.
The mesh is efficient at 215,453 polygons and 219,703 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and it arrives rigged so the gear retracts and the control surfaces move.

Two more rigged builds share this page at the same $329, prepared for Maya and for Cinema 4D. Aimed at business aviation marketing, charter and brokerage presentation, luxury travel advertising, airport visualisation and games.

This aircraft was designed from scratch for the hundred seat class rather than being shrunk from something larger, and it shows in the cabin: a wider seat on one side of the aisle than the other, larger windows and a genuinely different section from the older narrowbodies it competes with.

The model is built with subdivision geometry at 2,760,958 polygons and 2,876,799 vertices with non-overlapping UVs. Subdivision suits an airframe of long smooth curves, and the weight is largely the detailed interior.

A rigged build sits on this page at $319. The static model at $299 covers airline marketing, cabin and product visualisation, airport scenes, aviation journalism, film and television, and games. On sale since 2020.

A cable ship is organised around the cable path: over a bow sheave, through a linear engine amidships and down into enormous turntables in the hull. Above deck that gives a clear working area aft and a sheave at the bow that no other ship type carries.
The mesh runs 1,690,680 polygons and 1,886,547 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the density in the cable handling gear, the cranes and the deck fittings.

A rigged build sits on this page at $349. The static model at $299 covers subsea and telecommunications visualisation, offshore energy presentation, maritime industry marketing, documentary work and games. On sale since 2024.

A full car park is one of the most tedious things to assemble by hand and one of the most useful things to have ready. Fifty four bays with vehicles already placed, at varied angles and with realistic gaps, removes an afternoon of work from every urban render that needs a parking area.
It is a very large asset at 5,045,658 polygons and 5,410,801 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which is what a scene containing dozens of complete vehicles costs.

At $299 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits urban and architectural visualisation, property and development marketing, planning presentation, film and television, and games. On sale since 2025.

Social and documentary work often needs figures that architectural visualisation libraries do not provide: people who are not shoppers or commuters. This scene shows several figures gathered around a fire, and it exists so that material about housing, poverty and outreach can show the subject rather than abstract it.
The mesh runs 1,018,259 polygons and 953,630 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, covering the figures, their clothing and the fire they are gathered around.

At $299 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits documentary and journalism visualisation, social policy and charity communication, urban and film scenes, education material and games. On sale since 2025.

Big cats share a body plan but not a build: a lion, a tiger and a leopard differ in mass distribution, limb proportion and how the spine flexes at speed. A collection built as one family gets those differences right relative to each other, which separate purchases never quite do.
Every animal here arrives rigged and with fur grooming, which are the two things that take longest on a predator and the two things that most distinguish a convincing animal from a smooth model.
At $299 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits wildlife documentary and natural history, conservation and zoo material, advertising, film and television, and games. On sale since 2025.

Science fiction infantry work needs a squad rather than a hero. Several armoured figures with variation between them are what make a formation look like a unit instead of a cloned line, and every one here arrives rigged and prepared for Maya so posing and animation start immediately.

Building and rigging armoured characters is slow work, because armour plates have to move over a deforming body without intersecting it. Delivered solved, the set removes the longest part of that job.
At $295 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits games, science fiction film and television, cinematic previsualisation, concept work and illustration. On sale since 2026.

This ship carries a hull number in the cruiser series, and the naming reflects a fleet where the distinction between cruiser and destroyer became a matter of history rather than of size. What is visible is a modern surface combatant: fixed radar faces on the deckhouse, vertical launch decks fore and aft and a helicopter deck.
The mesh runs 1,382,544 polygons and 1,533,351 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the density in the superstructure, the mast array and the deck fittings.

At $289 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits naval and defence visualisation, documentary and news graphics, museum and commemorative material, film and television, and games. On sale since 2025.

Opening the life support backpack is what makes this asset unusual. A spacesuit is a spacecraft, and the pack on the back holds the oxygen, the cooling water, the carbon dioxide scrubber and the power - none of which is visible on a closed suit. Shown open, it explains the whole system.
The mesh runs 216,908 polygons and 231,131 vertices in quads and tris, and it arrives rigged. The UVs overlap, sensible on a suit with paired limbs and repeated fittings.

At $289 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits space industry and aerospace visualisation, documentary and museum material, education and training content, film and television, and games. On sale since 2026.

A product tanker is a hull covered in pipework. The deck carries the manifold amidships, cargo lines running fore and aft, vapour risers and a walkway above them, with the accommodation block and funnel right at the stern. That deck arrangement is what distinguishes a tanker from a bulk carrier at a glance.

This is among the largest assets in the catalogue at 7,365,517 polygons and 7,479,405 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and the density is exactly where it belongs: in the deck pipework and the fittings.

At $279 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits maritime and energy industry visualisation, port and terminal scenes, shipping and logistics presentation, documentary work and games. On sale since 2025.
